criteria_results.title: Identifies exclusive dealing claim (Sherman Act §1 and/or Clayton Act §3)
criteria_results.reasoning: Counts I and V are analyzed as exclusive dealing claims under Sherman Act 1 and Clayton Act 3, with reference to the ADA 7.2 70% requirement.

criteria_results.title: Identifies resale price maintenance (RPM) claim under Sherman Act §1
criteria_results.reasoning: Count II RPM is analyzed with reference to the 9.1 MAP clause and the 9.3 brand-positioning clause.

criteria_results.title: Identifies group boycott / concerted refusal to deal claim under Sherman Act §1
criteria_results.reasoning: Count III group boycott is analyzed, including the alleged coordination with Heartland and Great Lakes.

criteria_results.title: Identifies monopolization / attempted monopolization claim under Sherman Act §2
criteria_results.reasoning: Count IV, Section 2 monopolization and attempted monopolization, is analyzed in Part IV.D.

criteria_results.title: Identifies Illinois Antitrust Act state-law claim (740 ILCS 10/3)
criteria_results.reasoning: Count VI under 740 ILCS 10/3 is identified and analyzed separately in Part IV.E.

criteria_results.title: Identifies tortious interference with business relations claim
criteria_results.reasoning: Count VII tortious interference is identified and analyzed.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_001: Identifies implausible 72% gross margin in damages calculation
criteria_results.reasoning: The memo flags the 72% margin as unsupported, citing PH's actual 31.4% margin and the 28-35% industry range.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_001: Identifies methodological flaw in damages (margin on cost vs. revenue)
criteria_results.reasoning: The memo notes the margin was applied to the cost of goods purchased rather than to resale revenue.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_001: Provides corrected damages calculation reducing exposure
criteria_results.reasoning: The corrected figure is $3.11M per year and about $9.3M single (about $28M trebled), which is within the required range.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_002: Challenges narrow product market definition
criteria_results.reasoning: The memo challenges the organic-only product market, citing conventional and mixed suppliers that carry organic lines as evidence of substitution.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_002: Challenges arbitrary geographic market definition
criteria_results.reasoning: The memo states the six-state geographic market is unexplained and conclusory, which is a vulnerability.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_002: Notes broader market would reduce Greenfield's market share
criteria_results.reasoning: The memo never states that a broader market would cut Greenfield's share below 22%; it discusses only that a narrower market could raise the share.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_003: Identifies complaint's foreclosure calculation error (15.4%)
criteria_results.reasoning: The memo identifies that only 1,900 of 2,800 accounts (68%) have ADAs, so the 15.4% figure is overstated.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_003: Provides corrected foreclosure calculation (~10.46%)
criteria_results.reasoning: It gives 22% x 68% x 70% = about 10.5%.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_004: Applies rule of reason (not per se) to exclusive dealing
criteria_results.reasoning: It states exclusive dealing is judged under the rule of reason and cites Tampa Electric.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_004: Notes corrected foreclosure (~10.46%) is below actionable threshold
criteria_results.reasoning: It states the corrected figure of about 10% falls below the 30-40% foreclosure that courts generally look for.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_005: Distinguishes MAP policy (Section 9.1) from minimum RPM
criteria_results.reasoning: It explains that 9.1 restricts only advertised prices and expressly excludes transaction prices, which distinguishes MAP from RPM.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_005: Discusses Section 9.3 ambiguity and Alvarez email risk
criteria_results.reasoning: It discusses the 'sells' language in 9.3 and the Nov. 8, 2023 Alvarez email ('actually selling') as RPM exposure.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_006: Applies Leegin rule of reason to vertical RPM
criteria_results.reasoning: It applies the Leegin rule of reason to vertical minimum RPM.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_006: Recommends procompetitive justification defense for MAP/RPM
criteria_results.reasoning: It discusses free-riding prevention and brand positioning as procompetitive justifications under Leegin.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_007: Identifies insufficient factual basis for conspiracy/group boycott
criteria_results.reasoning: It notes the Complaint relies on parallel conduct, conference attendance and 'information and belief' allegations with no who, what or when, and on the Marsh email.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_007: Notes Heartland email supports independent business justification
criteria_results.reasoning: It explains that the Marsh email shows routine, conditional credit review after PH lost its largest supplier, which supports independent action.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_008: Applies Twombly plausibility standard to conspiracy claim
criteria_results.reasoning: It applies Twombly and the plus-factor requirement to the parallel-conduct and information-and-belief allegations.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_009: Identifies 22% market share as far below monopoly power threshold
criteria_results.reasoning: It states that 22% is far below the 50%+ threshold for monopoly power, citing Marshfield Clinic.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_009: Notes failure to allege dangerous probability for attempted monopolization
criteria_results.reasoning: It discusses the lack of a dangerous probability of success (below about 30%, with only 28.7% projected).

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_009: Assesses monopolization claim as low risk to Greenfield
criteria_results.reasoning: It rates Count IV 'very weak' and the highest-probability dismissal.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_010: Identifies HHI calculation error in the complaint
criteria_results.reasoning: It identifies that the Complaint merges the Big Three into one firm and treats the 36% fringe as a single firm.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_010: Provides corrected HHI calculation (~992 or similar)
criteria_results.reasoning: It computes 960 for the named firms and about 990 in total.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_011: Discusses 4-year statute of limitations under 15 U.S.C. §15b
criteria_results.reasoning: It discusses the four-year limitations period under 15 U.S.C. 15b.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_011: Identifies September 4, 2020 as the limitations cutoff date
criteria_results.reasoning: It never identifies Sept. 4, 2020 as the limitations cutoff or applies a cutoff to the claims.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_011: Notes Prairie Harvest ADA (Feb 2021) is within limitations period
criteria_results.reasoning: It does not analyze the Feb. 2021 ADA date against the limitations cutoff.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_011: Notes broader exclusivity program inception may raise limitations or continuing violation issues
criteria_results.reasoning: It does not discuss limitations issues for the Jan. 2020 program inception or the continuing violation doctrine.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_012: Flags Illinois Antitrust Act as requiring separate analysis
criteria_results.reasoning: It flags Illinois-specific issues (subsection specificity, trebling limits under 10/7(2), the fee provision, a possible Illinois RPM divergence) and the supplemental jurisdiction scenario if the federal claims fall.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_013: Addresses Prairie Harvest's antitrust standing
criteria_results.reasoning: It discusses antitrust injury (PH is a dealer, not a foreclosed rival) and PH's Clayton 16 standing for an injunction.

criteria_results.title: Recommends filing Rule 12(b)(6) motion to dismiss
criteria_results.reasoning: It recommends a comprehensive Rule 12(b)(6) motion.

criteria_results.title: Recommends 12(b)(6) dismissal of monopolization count (Section 2)
